Splitting up the integral into the sum of two integrals and evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2\cdot {3}^{x}+x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2\cdot {3}^{x}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}({3}^{1}-{3}^{0})+\frac{1}{2}({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(3-1)+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
